Cook visited Apple's Battersea campus in London this week and met with King Charles, as part of a new partnership between the company and The King's Trust.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also gave an in-depth interview to The Independent, discussing the partnership and his first month as Apple's executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO last month, handing the role to John Ternus. In this week's interview, Cook noted that the handover process actually began many years ago.

Ternus took over as CEO alongside the launch of the iPhone Duo, which Cook said had been fully planned well in advance. Cook explained: 'I wanted John to ride the momentum, and at Apple, momentum is basically built on the product cycle.'

Cook also stressed that as Apple's executive chairman, he focuses on 'global policy' matters, and mentioned he has 'very high trust' with Ternus. Cook is assisting Ternus 'in whatever way he sees fit,' but emphasised that he is not 'calling the shots.'

What advice has Cook given Ternus? 'Don't try to be me.' To read the full interview, visit The Independent's website. The article will also discuss Apple's latest partnership with The King's Trust.
